originalTitle: Pell slack splits exactly into magnitude shortfall and signed cancellation
originalHypotheses: Pell-window three-child recursion and a selected maximizing root window with its sign.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: For one exact child triple x,y,z, magnitude shortfall is2b_j+b_(j−1)−|x|−|y|−|z|≥0.
Writing P as positive mass and M as negative absolute mass gives cancellation P+M−|P−M|=2min(P,M)≥0.
Adding gives Short+Cancel=2b_j+b_(j−1)−|W_(j+1)(s)|. Bounded integer window defects attain their maxima, so minimizing over starts gives S_j=2b_j+b_(j−1)−b_(j+1).
The identity S=Short+Cancel applies at a parent maximizer (or after taking minimum), not indiscriminately at every start. S=0 requires all child norms saturated and no nonzero opposite-sign child.
For δ=min(2,S/max(1,b)), δb≤S even at b=0, so the cumulative-transfer premise follows ifΣδ diverges. Divergence itself is not proved by the identity.
